label: bug-fix effect only, on unchanged data (main, self-reported vs main, dedup-recomputed)
notes: One-off audit, not a normal pipeline comparison. main's tree.json predates the multi-parent-category dedup fix, so its own reported root.stats double-counted 130 pages that were already filed under 2+ categories. This entry compares main's original self-reported stats ('old') against the same main data with today's dedup-by-page-id logic manually applied ('new') -- no live-data change at all, isolating the pure effect of correcting the counting bug. From the next changelog entry onward, root.stats is always dedup-correct at generation time, so this kind of manual audit is never needed again.

label: live-data growth only, clean-to-clean (main dedup-recomputed vs current branch tip)
notes: One-off, not a normal pipeline comparison. 'old' is main's dedup-recomputed baseline from the previous changelog entry (259,163,815 bytes / 4,522 pages), not main's own (buggy) root.stats. 'new' is the current branch tip's root.stats, already dedup-correct. Both sides are deduped, so this delta isolates pure live-Wikisource-data growth (new/edited pages) between the main snapshot and today, with no bug-fix effect mixed in -- that effect was isolated separately in the previous entry. Page-level last-edited-date comparison is not possible against main: that snapshot predates the last_changed field entirely, so '0 pages with a changed timestamp' below reflects a schema gap, not a confirmed absence of edits. Page added/removed counts ARE meaningful (both sides have page ids).

label: subpage descent enabled: newly discovered content, not a data-quality bug
notes: This entry marks the pipeline transition where scrape.py started descending into MediaWiki subpages (Title/Subtitle, e.g. an index/ToC page's linked chapter pages) via list=allpages, in addition to the category-tree walk it already did. 'old' is the branch tip's tree.json from just before this change (last real content-side entry: #2, live-data growth). 'new' is the first run with subpage descent enabled by default. This produced a large jump (+14,159 pages, +122.9% bytes) that is entirely newly-discovered REAL content that already existed on Wikisource, not duplication or a bug: many works are organized as a small index/ToC page (invisible in byte count) linking to dozens of full-content subpages that categorymembers alone never saw (see CLAUDE.md's नैषधीयचरितम् case study for a worked example, and the बैबल् case for why this was previously gated off by default -- it originally tripped Wikimedia's rate limiter, since fixed by both a --subpage-delay pacing knob and, more importantly, giving the scraper's User-Agent proper contact info so it qualifies for Wikimedia's higher-rate-limit tier (10 req/min unidentified vs 200 req/min compliant), per https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_APIs/Rate_limits). All 4,625 pre-existing pages are unchanged (0 removed, 0 with a different last_changed timestamp) -- this is purely additive discovery. After this entry, subpage descent is permanent (no opt-out flag), so further scrapes go back to being ordinary compare.py runs, same as any other rerun.
